items.q: 'Snake-Hips' Tucker was a tough guy and loved to fight. When he did his number the customers would throw dollar bills on the floor just to see him do a summersault and go into a split to pick them up.

ctx.x: section consisted of Glyn Pague and Henry 'Moon' Jones on altos, Bingie Madison tenor. Jimmy Arckey was still there on trombone and Lee Blaire played guitar.

'Snake-Hips' Tucker was a tough guy and loved to fight. When he did his number the customers would throw dollar bills on the floor just to see him do a summersault and go into a split to pick them up. One night a table of college guys were with some girls and one of these fellows heated a half-dollar and threw it on the floor. 'Snake' didn't know that the piece was hot but he found out when he picked it up. 'Snake' finished his dance near the table where the smart alec had thrown the hot half-dollar and hit the…

Connie was a reasonable fellow but did not stand for his show people to be abused. And the waiters were tough also so no client could get away with whatever they thought they could with the entertainers or the orchestra when their drinks got too heavy for them to carry.
